name: Surveyor 3 lander

location.name: Oceanus Procellarum (Ocean of Storms), beside the Apollo 12 site

headline: A robot lander that waited 2½ years for visitors, who took its camera home
story: In the first minutes of 20 April 1967, Surveyor 3 reached the Ocean of Storms and would not stay down. Reflective rocks confused its radar, its engines kept firing, and the lander bounced twice before settling on a 14-degree slope inside a crater about 200 meters across.

For two weeks it photographed its surroundings, returning 6,326 pictures, and dug trenches up to 18 centimeters deep with a small scoop on an extending arm. Then the lunar night fell. Its last data arrived on 4 May 1967, and it never woke again.

In November 1969, Apollo 12 landed less than 200 meters away. On their second moonwalk, Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walked to the crater and removed about 10 kilograms of parts, including the television camera and the scoop, so scientists could study how the Moon had changed them. The rest of Surveyor 3 still stands on the crater slope.

facts.label: Brought home by Apollo 12
facts.value: About 10 kg, including the TV camera and scoop

images.caption: November 1969: Pete Conrad examines Surveyor 3's television camera before detaching it. Apollo 12's lunar module stands in the background.
